pr_title: buffer: refactor `byteLength` to remove outdated optimizations
pr_body:
The third argument `mustMatch` is now outdated, so remove it.

Fixes: https://github.com/nodejs/node/issues/38536
pr_comments: Marking semver-major out of caution in case `mustMatch` is used somewhere in the ecosystem. @nodejs/tsc
CITGM results seem fine to me, although I wouldn't mind it if someone more familiar with evaluating CITGM results took a look.
The Jenkins CI results are from 10 months ago, so I'm going to re-run them.
The way shared-libs-debug keeps failing to build in CI can't actually be related to this, can it?

I'm going to rebase against master, force push to the branch, and rerun CI to see if it fixes anything. CI is supposed to be rebasing against master, but maybe it's not or something.....

issue_context.title: `Buffer.byteLength`'s implementation is not consistent with the documentation
issue_context.body:
https://github.com/nodejs/node/blob/f71166bfa222d41020d76aec3dd9b77214324627/lib/buffer.js#L729-L752

In line 741 it checks the third argument `mustMatch`, which is not mentioned in [the document](https://nodejs.org/api/buffer.html#buffer_static_method_buffer_bytelength_string_encoding)

So I guess either the implementation or the documentation should be updated.
comments: I believe it was part of a now outdated optimization. I think it can be removed from the code (the parts where `mustMatch` would've been `true`).

review_comments: Why is the test being removed? Do we not still want to make sure the behavior is unchanged?
Oh, I see, there is no third argument. Never mind, I get it.
